newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse ends down in scandal sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse ends down in scandal sell-off.

text.p: The Athens bourse, rocked by a settlement scandal that halted trade for almost four days, closed 3.31 percent down after a day of steady selling in low to moderate turnover.
It was the first normal session since the scandal and brokers and analysts predicted that the fall would continue for a few days.
The crisis was triggered last week when Delta Securities tried to settle its account at the bourse clearing house with bad cheques.
"Fundamentally, nothing has changed. Today's sell-off had a big psychological component and it might take some time before the wounds are healed," said a floor trader who requested anonymity.he said.
"Optimism is a scarce commodity in times such as these but this episode could well turn out to be a blessing in disguise in the medium turn leading to a stronger, healthier market," he said.
The bourse closed 3.31 percent or 30.04 points lower at 878.38 points after opening at 908.07. Turnover was moderate at 5.019 billion drachmas.

Losers led gainers 175 to 18 with 14 issues unchanged on 207 traded. Banks lost 3.71 percent, industrials closed 3.66 percent lower with construction plunging 6.70 percent. Small-caps climbed 3.79 percent.

ING Barings said in its daily commentary that the bourse authorities would have to come up with a plan to avoid similar crises in the future and the government appeared more determined to get tougher with brokers who fail to settle on time.

The 65-member Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEXA), angered by perceived inaction by the authorities to probe the Delta scandal, refused to trade last Friday and effectively closed the bourse for four days.
Bourse authorities on Thursday ordered a two-day suspension in trade in four stocks linked to the Delta settlement scandal.
"The suspension is not related to the companies or their financial situation but will facilitate any possible checks being conducted on transactions in their shares to date," a bourse statement said.
The national economy ministry has ordered an audit of 10 brokerages.
